correspondences.rationale: Both denote hard failure of a coherent transmitter's laser.
Both denote failure of an equipment card as a hard fault.
Both denote receiver-local degradation that adds a signal penalty.
Both denote incipient transmit-laser ageing manifested by upward bias-current drift.
Both denote a slow decline in an optical channel's operating margin.
Both denote a physical fibre cut that prevents light from passing.
Both denote a hard amplifier or pump failure producing no optical output.
Both denote disconnection of a patch cord or connector that opens the optical path.
Both denote increased fibre-span attenuation from damage, bends, or splice loss.
Both denote an amplifier noise-figure increase that lowers downstream OSNR.
Both denote increased differential group delay on the fibre path.
Both denote frequency offset of a WSS passband for one channel.
Both denote a rapid transient change in optical state of polarization.
Both denote connector contamination that introduces optical loss or penalty.
Both serve as generic placeholders for an unspecified failure upstream on the relevant signal path.
Both denote amplifier gain falling below its configured target.
Both denote incipient pump ageing manifested by increasing drive current.
Both denote non-flat wavelength-dependent amplifier gain.

Both denote failure of a client port or its optic.

Both denote a nonfunctional equipment unit that can no longer carry traffic or provide valid monitoring.
Both denote a fast state-of-polarization change.

Both denote rising transmit-laser bias current as the observable ageing condition.

Both denote pump current rising to maintain amplifier gain.

Both denote an ODU delivered to the wrong destination by a cross-connect.

Both denote optical power measured at a line receiver.

Both denote an amplifier at the receiving end of an OMS.

Both denote a client-facing port that maps a client signal into an ODU.

Both denote the remote line transmitter sending toward the observing unit.
